meta.title: Flint
meta.description: 39.8B-parameter (2.5B active) MoE with hybrid sliding-window / full attention, reasoning and tool calling; BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints on a single Blackwell GPU.
meta.performance_headline: Single GB200, NVFP4: ~2.0 ms per output token at batch 1 with 100K context

recommended_command.docker_command:
docker run --gpus all \
  --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  vllm/vllm-openai:latest RecursiveSI/flint \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none \
  --reasoning-parser glm47

strategy_spec.name: single_node_tp
strategy_spec.description: Single-node tensor parallel. Splits the model across all local GPUs. TP size is set to the GPU count at deploy time. The simplest multi-GPU strategy — works for all model architectures.

hardware_profile.description: NVIDIA GB200 Grace-Blackwell compute tray · 192 GB HBM3e/GPU · 4 Blackwell GPUs (NVL72 tray unit)

pip.command:
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -U vllm --torch-backend auto
pip.note: Use a nightly wheel. The NVFP4 GGUF checkpoint also needs `pip install 'gguf>=0.19.0'`.

tool_calling.description: Automatic tool choice with the GLM-4.7 XML tool-call parser (Flint's chat template emits <tool_call>/<arg_key>/<arg_value>); tools are dropped from the prompt when tool_choice is none, as in the reference runtime.

reasoning.description: Return the <think>…</think> block in the reasoning field; the model decides per turn whether to reason.

nvfp4.description: NVFP4 GGUF served weight-only (W4A16); 23.5 GB resident after load (the LM head is dequantized to BF16). Config and tokenizer come from the BF16 repo.

guide:
## Overview

Flint is a 39.8B-parameter mixture-of-experts model (256 experts, top-6 sigmoid routing plus a
shared expert; ~2.5B parameters active per token) with 49 layers: 35 sliding-window layers
(window 513, RoPE) and 14 full-attention layers (no RoPE), GQA 32/4, attention sinks, and a
262,144-token context. Two checkpoints are served:

- [RecursiveSI/flint](https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint): BF16 safetensors.
- [RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf](https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf): a single
  NVFP4 GGUF (repacked losslessly at load and run as W4A16, like the reference runtime). It ships
  no config or tokenizer; both come from the BF16 repo.

Tested end to end on one GB200 (TP=1, BF16 KV cache, CUDA graphs, no torch.compile) for both
checkpoints. On a single GPU the Flint kernels are always used (fused MoE, small-batch CuTe GEMV,
CuTe decode attention, low-latency decode path for <= 8 requests); TP > 1 and expert parallelism
fall back to stock vLLM layers and are not validated.

## Launch

BF16:

```bash
vllm serve RecursiveSI/flint --served-model-name flint \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none
```

NVFP4 (requires `gguf>=0.19.0`):

```bash
vllm serve RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf \
  --hf-config-path RecursiveSI/flint --tokenizer RecursiveSI/flint \
  --served-model-name flint \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none
```

## Client usage

Use `/v1/chat/completions`. Sampling defaults from `generation_config.json`: temperature 1.0,
top_p 0.95, top_k 20 (greedy decoding is not validated). Reasoning is returned in `reasoning`
and counts toward `max_tokens`; use `max_tokens` of at least 32768 for hard problems.

```bash
curl localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "flint",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17*23? Answer briefly."}],
  "max_tokens": 1024
}'
```

Accuracy on GB200 with this recipe (BF16 / NVFP4): GSM8K 0.950 / 0.950, GPQA-Diamond (4 repeats)
0.721 / 0.696, MRCR (48 samples, up to 114K-token prompts) ~0.47 / ~0.46, tool-calling suite
(19 cases x 10: typed args, tool selection, parallel calls, multi-turn, tool_choice none,
escaping, streaming) 10/10 on every case.

## Benchmarking

Forward time on one GB200 (`vllm bench forward`, batch x context, us):

| shape | BF16 | NVFP4 |
|---|---|---|
| decode 1 x 100K | 2341 | 1783 |
| decode 8 x 100K | 6836 | 5703 |
| decode 32 x 100K | 19580 | 16716 |
| prefill 8K @ 100K | 145617 | 144765 |

Serving (NVFP4, `vllm bench serve`, random 1000 in / 1000 out): TPOT 2.0 ms at concurrency 1,
2.8 ms at 8, 4.9 ms at 32, 8.5 ms at 128; median inter-token latency 2.06 ms at batch 1 with
100K context. Prefill runs eagerly and is CPU-bound on kernel-launch overhead: TTFT is ~60 ms
for a short prompt and ~125 ms for an 8K-token prompt.

## Troubleshooting

- Rust frontend: not supported for this recipe. It rejects `--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none`,
  and for NVFP4 also `--hf-config-path` / `--tokenizer`; keep the default Python frontend.
- Reasoning parser: the reference runtime's `deepseek-v3` name maps to vLLM's `deepseek_v3`
  parser, which only extracts reasoning when the request enables `thinking`; with Flint the
  reasoning then stays in `content`. Use `glm47`.
- If `content` contains literal `<think>` or `<tool_call>` text, the server was started without
  the parsers above.
- Batch-1 decode time varies by ~3-4% between sessions (a GPU-side state, not configuration).
